value.rationale: Two exact measurements is a natural finite computational budget when refining simulated Brownian bridges to catch a negative excursion missed by an endpoint-only discretization. The theorem proves a universal strict reversal of the intuitive centered-first decision even though midpoint is the unique optimum with one query; a closed Gamma-function cusp coefficient quantifies the effect for every positive clearance, and the conditional second-query rule is explicit. This is a structural design boundary, not just a numerical fact about an arbitrary parameter slice. At c=1/2 the concrete t=1/3 first query improves detection probability by roughly 4.56% over t=1/2.
